title: Winchester / Clark County seat

bodyMarkdown:
Winchester grew up on John Baker's land after a year of decisions by the justices of Clark County, created by the Kentucky General Assembly in 1792. The Assembly acted on December 6, 1792, and named the county for George Rogers Clark. A [Winchester Sun history column on the town's name](https://winchestersun.com/2023/04/29/enoch-origin-of-the-name-winchester/) walks through the court records that followed.

## Before the county

Long before settlers arrived, the Shawnee town of Eskippakithiki stood about 11 miles southeast of present-day Winchester. The [Grokipedia entry on Clark County](https://grokipedia.com/page/Clark_County,_Kentucky) says its people used the area for seasonal hunting, corn growing and trade along warrior paths, and that the town was abandoned around 1750. Its later history is told in [the Odawa raid at Eskippakithiki](/stories/odawa-raid-at-eskippakithiki-1753/).

Settler stations came in the late 1770s. Grokipedia credits John Strode with founding Strode's Station nearby in 1779.

## Choosing a site

The 1792 act told the new county's justices to meet at John Strode's house and "fix upon a place to hold courts." Later that month Governor Isaac Shelby appointed the first justices. They included John Baker, Enoch Smith and Hubbard Taylor, among others. They did not meet until March 1793.

At a later session the justices voted by ballot, and a majority chose to put the public buildings on Baker's land. A committee was told to pick the exact spot. In October it announced the site of John Baker's spring, which became an important water source in the town's early years. The justices then met for the first time at Baker's house.

## The town is established

The legislature then passed an act establishing a town on Baker's land "to be known by the name of Winchester." The Sun gives the date as December 17, 1793. The [Grokipedia entry on Winchester](https://grokipedia.com/page/Winchester,_Kentucky) gives December 19, 1793, and says Baker donated 66 acres.

In January Baker objected that the low ground near the spring was a poor place for a courthouse. The justices agreed and moved the public buildings to the ridge "before John Baker's door." A two-room log courthouse went up in 1794 and was replaced by a two-story brick building in 1797.

## Where the name came from

Grokipedia says the town was named for Baker's hometown of Winchester, Virginia. The Sun column traces that story to the Clark County Chronicles, published in the 1920s. Its author found a John Baker living in Winchester, Virginia, in 1788 but could not prove he was the same man. The Virginia origin is plausible but not proven.

## Kentucky today

Winchester remains the Clark County seat. Its local food fame is beer cheese, a spread invented in the late 1930s at the nearby Driftwood Inn. Kentucky recognized Clark County as its place of origin in 2013, and Winchester holds a festival in its honor.
